court: In the High Court of Madras†
respondents: State of Tamil Nadu, Rep. by its Secretary to Government, Home Department and Others
case_number: W.P. Crl.(MD) No. 3220 of 2026 and W.P.M.P. Crl.(MD) No. 779 of 2026
advocates: For R 1, R 2, R 3 & R 5 : M/s. M.R. Priyanka Jothi
For R 4 & R 6 : Mr. D. Rajaboopathy
judgment_text:
PRAYER : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of writ of mandamus, to direct the respondents 1 to 6 (i) to forthwith transfer the body of the petitioner's deceased mother, namely, Tmt. Panjavarnam, from the Government Medical College Hospital, Sivagangai to any other Government Medical College Hospital outside Sivagangai District, preferably Government Rajaji Hospital, Madurai or to such other Government Medical College Hospital as this Court may deem fit and proper; (ii) to conduct the postmortem examination only through an Independent Medical Board consisting of not less than three Senior Forensic Medicine Experts having no connection whatsoever with the 7th respondent; (iii) to conduct and complete the entire postmortem examination under continuous videography from commencement till completion and preserve the original video recording; (iv) to ensure that the identification of the body, conduct of postmortem examination, collection and sealing of viscera, blood samples, tissue samples, stomach contents, injection-site tissues and all other forensic materials are carried out under the supervision of the jurisdictional Judicial Magistrate or such judicial officer as may be nominated by the competent court; (v) to preserve the complete treatment records, inpatient records, case sheets, prescriptions, nursing notes, medicine administration records, investigation reports, con sent forms, registers, CCTV footage and all other connected records available with Hemalatha Hospital, Kalaiyarkovil; (vi) to ensure a fair, impartial, independent and effective investigation in Crime No. 260 of 2026 dated 13-6-2026 on the file of the 6th respondent police and to take further action in accordance with law based upon the outcome of the postmortem report, forensic reports and investigation.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

L. Victoria Gowri, J.:— Seeking the direct the respondents 2 and 5 to conduct the postmortem examination of the petitioner's deceased mother, namely, Tmt. Panjavarnam only through a Board consisting of not less than three Senior Forensic Medicine Experts with mandatory videography of the entire procedure and preservation of viscera, blood samples, tissue samples, stomach contents, injection-site tissues and all other forensic materials, this writ petition is filed.

2. Since no adverse order is passed against the private respondent, notice to the private respondent is dispensed with.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that due to the wrong treatment given by the 7th respondent, the petitioner's mother had died. In this regard, to substantiate her claim, she had made an application to conduct a postmortem of her mother with a properly constituted Board. Since the same was not considered, the petitioner filed this writ petition.

4. The learned government advocate(Civil Side) on oral instructions, submitted that the 7th respondent has already been suspended from service and hence, the question of fearing that he would conduct the postmortem will not arise.

5. Heard the learned counsel on either side and carefully perused the materials available on record.

6. Though the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that a team of doctors from another Medical College should conduct the postmortem of her mother, since the learned government advocate (Civil Side) submitted that the 7th respondent has already been suspended from service, the question of the petitioner's fear that the postmortem would be conducted by the same doctor is baseless. In view of the same, making it clear that the postmortem should be conducted on the body of Tmt. Panjavarnam on 18-6-2026 by a team of doctors other than the 7th respondent, this writ petition is disposed of. It is directed to conduct the said postmortem under continuous videography from commencement till completion and preserve the original video recording.

7. With the above directions, this Writ Petition stands disposed of. Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
